decisions.title: Project claim level and public name
decisions.rationale: The project will first establish a causal, configuration-specific result for a DeepSeek Harness plugin. Broader framework language must be earned through cross-model, cross-harness, and cross-task evidence.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Prematurely broadens scope, increases confounding, and would overstate evidence before external-validity studies.
Would remove the central online termination-control and repair contribution.

decisions.title: Primary estimand and endpoint family

options.summary: Exit calibration: FAR reduction with FCR non-inferiority

decisions.rationale: False Accept and False Continue directly measure whether the termination controller is better calibrated. Certified Success and Repair Conversion remain important secondary outcomes; exact margins and thresholds require later independent methods review.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Final pass rate alone cannot isolate termination quality, corrupt success, or simple extra-compute effects.
Judge agreement validates an evaluator but does not establish system usefulness.
A composite would introduce arbitrary weights and allow hard failures to be compensated by unrelated gains.

decisions.title: Hypothesis hierarchy

options.summary: RQ4 primary; RQ1 foundational; RQ5-RQ6 secondary; RQ2-RQ3 method; RQ7 external

decisions.rationale: The hierarchy preserves the evidence chain from information value to auditability, calibration, repair, system benefit, and finally external validity while controlling multiplicity.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Treating every question as co-primary creates an unnecessary multiplicity and interpretation burden.
A final-success-only claim would skip mechanism, audit reliability, and calibration evidence needed to interpret the result.

decisions.title: Initial model, harness, and task-stream scope

options.summary: DeepSeek-V4-Pro + fixed DSH; Stream V first

decisions.rationale: A fixed DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek Harness development configuration with highly verifiable tasks gives the cleanest mechanism test. Semi-open tasks and external configurations follow after reliable labels and interfaces exist.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Immediate breadth would slow mechanism development and make causal attribution difficult.
Semi-open tasks do not provide sufficiently strong initial ground truth for auditor calibration.

decisions.title: Certified Success and hard process violations

options.summary: Dual certification with hard process gates

decisions.rationale: Trusted success requires both outcome completion and satisfaction of non-compensatory authorization, integrity, mandatory-precondition, and current-evidence rules. No additional P0 hard gates were added beyond the drafted list.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Outcome-only acceptance cannot detect corrupt success or unauthorized and integrity-violating paths.
A compliant process cannot substitute for an outcome that did not satisfy the goal.

decisions.title: Completion authority
decisions.rationale: Separating PROPOSED_COMPLETE from COMPLETE removes circular worker self-certification while retaining scalable autonomous benchmark execution.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Preserves the exact self-evaluation and premature-exit problem under study.
Creates an unnecessary human bottleneck for every verifiable benchmark completion.

decisions.title: Trace and reasoning-data policy

options.summary: Observable trace + structured checkpoints; no private CoT requirement

decisions.rationale: Observable events, tool outcomes, state changes, evidence links, and short structured checkpoints are auditable and portable. Worker explanations remain claims rather than self-authenticating evidence.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Full textual reasoning has faithfulness, privacy, availability, and cross-model comparability risks.
Tool calls alone may not expose unsupported obligation promotion or evidence interpretation errors.

decisions.title: Human role assignments and separation
decisions.rationale: Early development may combine Research Owner, Domain Lead, and Data Steward under RichardCao06. Independent methods review is mandatory before confirmatory protocol freeze, and a separate Independent Custodian is mandatory before any sealed evaluator or sealed test is created, accessed, or unsealed.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Full separation is desirable but not required for reversible P1 development and would unnecessarily block the project at P0.
Permanent single-person control cannot support strong confirmatory, sealed-test, or independent-approval claims.

Methods / Statistics Lead.deadline: Before confirmatory protocol freeze or approval of primary margins, thresholds, exclusions, and sample design

Independent Custodian.deadline: Before any held-out or sealed evaluator material is created, accessed, hashed for release, or unsealed

decisions.title: Sealed-data and hidden-evaluator boundary
decisions.rationale: Hidden evaluators may label copied candidate-stop snapshots offline, but detailed hidden failures cannot enter Worker or online Auditor context. Oracle feedback is permitted only as a separately labeled upper-bound condition.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Would confound process certification with privileged benchmark-oracle access.
Would prevent credible held-out and generalization claims.

decisions.title: Human–Agent collaboration and repository governance

options.summary: Adopt draft protocol and PR governance

decisions.rationale: PR-based Work Orders, decision records, role separation, failure preservation, deterministic checks, and amendments make research changes visible and reduce post-result drift.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Informal chat decisions are difficult to audit, freeze, and distinguish from post hoc changes.
Allowing an Agent to approve normative rules conflicts with the project's own separation-of-authority principle.
